subject: Prod-grade model pinning & audit trail for Celesta
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Huang <tim.h@celesta.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: deterministic model pinning + audit trail for Celesta deal

Tim — great speaking earlier. As promised, I’m outlining Celesta’s core ask so we can scope engineering impact and a timeline. High-level: Celesta needs deterministic model pinning per customer (ability to lock a tenant to an explicit model build + tokenizer/quantization metadata) and an immutable audit trail that records model version, prompt hash, response snapshot, and routing decision for every production request for a rolling 12-month retention window.

Business driver: Celesta is regulated (payment data in scope) and their auditors will require the ability to reproduce outputs tied to a fixed model for past transactions and to trace which model produced a given response. They want this in the contract as an SLA appendix — see attached SLA-Appendix-Celesta.pdf and our mutual action plan.

Asks from Redwood:
- Feasibility confirmation (eng estimate + risk list)
- Rough ETA for a minimal viable solution (pin + exportable audit logs) and a full solution (pin + searchable, per-tenant retention + retention config)
- Any gating product decisions (e.g., changes to routing, storage, or retention UI/UX)

Timeline: Celesta has requested a contractor kickoff by the end of Q2 (they want a pilot in July). They’ve signaled willingness to sign a 12-month committed capacity if we can commit to a delivery window; they’re also asking for a 10% concession if this is delivered as part of the initial go-live.

cc’ing Marissa (CS lead) to keep customer success and implementation aligned. Thanks — I’ll consolidate replies into a short one-pager for procurement.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0183
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: deterministic model pinning + audit trail for Celesta deal

Sergio — thanks for the clear write-up. High level reactions from engineering:

1) Pinning: technically straightforward if we support an explicit model_version identifier on the routing layer and prevent automatic rollouts for pinned tenants. Work roughly splits across: routing policy change (store/resolve tenant pin), runtime validation to ensure pinned model artifact is available on serving pool, and console/API UI to set/remove pins.

2) Audit trail: the exportable log you describe is heavier. Storing a per-request snapshot (prompt hash, model_version, tokenizer metadata, response hash, trace id) is doable, but retention + searchable index for 12 months will have storage and cost implications. We’ll need optionality: cold storage export vs. hot searchable index.

Open questions:
- Do we need cryptographic immutability (append-only hash chain) or is an exportable signed log sufficient for auditors?
- What retention SLA (12 months vs. 24 months) and read frequency (monthly audit vs. on-demand)?
- Is Celesta ok with a per-request metadata log + periodic bulk exports to their bucket, or do they require Redwoods-hosted searchable retention?

Estimate (rough):
- MVP (pin + basic request metadata + export job to S3): 6–8 weeks (small eng + one backend + one infra)
- Full (pin + searchable 12-month retention + UI + consoles + docs): 12–16 weeks and non-trivial storage cost ops.

I’ll put a short tech risks list together if we move forward. Markus — can you advise on infra/costs for a 12-month searchable store vs export-only?

— Karthik
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Timothy Huang <tim.h@celesta.io>, Celesta Procurement <procurement@celesta.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: deterministic model pinning + audit trail for Celesta deal

Tim — thanks for the time last week. To clarify on the audit side: their compliance team needs the ability to request a full per-transaction export for a given date range (example: all responses generated March 1–31, 2028) and to receive a CSV/NDJSON export that includes model_version, prompt_id, prompt_hash, response_hash, and a signed manifest describing the model artifact. For day-one pilot they don’t need a searchable UI, but they do need the export to be available on demand and delivered to their S3.

From our side: we can scope an MVP that implements pinning + per-request metadata capture + scheduled and on-demand S3 export. That maps to Karthik’s MVP estimate.

Commercial: we can tentatively accept the 10% concession if they commit to a 12-month reserved capacity at the Enterprise tier. Procurement — if this aligns, can you confirm contract language required for the SLA appendix (I attached a draft appendix for your redlines)?

— Marissa
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: deterministic model pinning + audit trail for Celesta deal

Quick infra notes:
- Storage: estimate 200–400 GB/month for metadata-only (no full response bodies) for an expected Celesta volume of ~10M tokens/month. If they want response snapshots included, multiply by ~4–6x depending on compression.
- Cost: hot searchable retention for 12 months ~ $Xk/month (we’ll provide a more precise number after a sizing run). Export-only to customer S3 is ~30% of that.
- Ops: we’ll need retention policies + lifecycle jobs and a customer-managed S3 target to reduce our long-term storage liability.

Blockers:
1) API to set pin needs authentication & audit in console (product work)
2) Export pipeline needs DLP review if responses are included (security)

If product wants us to build MVP in 6–8 weeks, we need a clear acceptance criteria doc, target S3 details, and a signed MSA addendum that states export SLAs and retention window.

— Markus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Timothy Huang <tim.h@celesta.io>, Celesta Legal <legal@celesta.io>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: deterministic model pinning + audit trail for Celesta deal

Team — thank you. This thread is now the ask summary I’ll share with Procurement and Legal at Celesta. Next steps I’ll own:
- Sergio: produce a one-page acceptance criteria doc and send to Celesta procurement by Tue 20 Apr
- Marissa: prepare the commercial note (10% concession as conditional on 12-month reserved capacity)
- Karthik + Markus: please confirm we can commit to the 6–8 week MVP timeline for pin + per-request metadata + S3 export if Celesta signs the addendum. If there are objections to the ETA please flag them in-thread by EOD Mon 19 Apr.

Tim / Legal — if this sounds aligned we’ll follow up with the acceptance criteria and a revised appendix for redline. Appreciate the quick turnaround — Celesta is a large strategic account for Q3.

— Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
